### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, touching **23** documentable anchor(s).

**16** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 45e9b2f14c91f76683296cd33bb1b477cbaef1bb`.

⛔ **10** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 45e9b2f14c91f76683296cd33bb1b477cbaef1bb` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `8b637dfc0518317d30f055f0572df2dfa5d5897e` — the merge of head `8604d1dc074b61a9240294ed18dc5a22eebf9c26` into base `45e9b2f14c91f76683296cd33bb1b477cbaef1bb`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 8b637dfc0518317d30f055f0572df2dfa5d5897e && git checkout 8b637dfc0518317d30f055f0572df2dfa5d5897e
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 45e9b2f14c91f76683296cd33bb1b477cbaef1bb 8604d1dc074b61a9240294ed18dc5a22eebf9c26 && git checkout -B drift-repro 45e9b2f14c91f76683296cd33bb1b477cbaef1bb && git merge --no-ff 8604d1dc074b61a9240294ed18dc5a22eebf9c26

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 45e9b2f14c91f76683296cd33bb1b477cbaef1bb
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 45e9b2f14c91f76683296cd33bb1b477cbaef1bb` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `7d6842b30a5006dd6d1edbd2a6858af2104f6611`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-save-door-refusals.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-authoring-gate.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.unknown-grant-object-refusal.test.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.restore-doors-save-refusal-family.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/permission-unknown-grant-object-refusal.dogfood.test.ts, scripts/engine-double-contract.pinned.json + packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts (`collectPermissionGrantObjectErrors`, `isPlatformObjectName`, read on `main`), packages/objectql/src/registry.ts (`getObject` / `resolveObjectKey`), packages/core/src/security/effective-object-permissions.ts (the evaluator keys a grant by object name), `.changeset/26724-object-unknown-datasource-refused.md` (the precedent)

Rendered by the seat's subagent, read-only, at 2026-11-02T07:22Z: card #28990 (body, triage, the seat's claim), PR #29093 (body, 8 files, net diff vs `origin/main` `5d3667e2`, merge-base `0be247ce`), the head's 46 check-runs, and the cited code at the head.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept-set narrowing (right).** `saveMetaItem` (draft and live, `force` included), `promoteDraftForPublish` (behind `publishMetaItem` and `publishPackageDrafts`) and `refuseRestoredBodyTheSaveDoorRefuses` (rollback, commit revert) now refuse a `permission` body whose `objects` key names no object the runtime knows; accepted 200 on `main`. The envelope is the schema gate's own (`422 INVALID_METADATA`, `issues[{path:'objects.NAME', code:'custom'}]`, message built by `specValidationFindings`): no new code, no new gate. Matches ruling 3 and the #26724 shape line for line.
- **"Known" (right).** `'*'` → exempt (the evaluator's wildcard, `effective-object-permissions.ts`); `registry.getObject(key)?.name === key` (the real `getObject` also answers a legacy `pkg__name` FQN and an ambiguous short name's first match; equality on `.name` rejects the FQN spelling the evaluator never keys by — correct, since `checkObjectPermission` indexes `objects[objectName]`); `readMetaItem({type:'object'})` (stored row, else code layer); on a draft save any object draft; on a package publish the batch's object drafts (`batchObjects`, built beside `batchDatasources`, passed only from `publishPackageDrafts`). A registry without `getObject` refuses nothing — the precedent's conservative default.
- **Held-grant exemption (right, and required by ruling 3).** Keys the set's current active definition already holds are not judged, so `os migrate meta --stored` (re-saves through `saveMetaItem`), the org-ownership ceremony and a restore that keeps the grant pass; a restore that re-introduces a grant the current set dropped is refused (pinned in the restore family test and the dogfood rollback case).
- **Public surface: none moved.** `SaveDoorRefusalHost` / `AuthoringGateHost` are not exported from `index.ts`; the class gains one `private` method and `promoteDraftForPublish` (private) one optional request member. `engine-double-contract.pinned.json` is generated output (ledger for the new test double), not reviewed.
- **Check-runs at review time:** 34 completed, all `success` or `skipped`, none failed; 12 still running: Test Core 1/8–8/8, Build Core, Lint & Repo Gates, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · workspace. The dogfood regression gate and the dogfood verify CLI are `success`/`skipped` on this head. CI's conclusions govern those still running.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/28990-permission-grant-unknown-object.md`: `@objectstack/metadata-protocol: minor`, BREAKING banner, `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` on both the PR body and the changeset, ADR-0087 `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` with its reason. Identical in level and shape to the #26724 changeset (`minor`, narrowing, no migration). The diff ships only in `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` (the dogfood test and the pinned ledger ship in no package). `Check Changeset` and `check-changeset-no-major` green. Right.

Clause-②: no (narrowing) — matches the diff: nothing is widened, nothing is added to any schema; one stored-before shape is now refused at every door that writes a permission set.

### ③ Boundary flags

- "Out of scope: `fields` keys (`object.field`) not judged; a translation's `objects.no_such_object` also saves 200" — answered: neither is this card's reach (the card names the permission set's `objects` map); the translation observation is a new card's, not escalated here.
- "`check:dual-build-cjs-loads` exit 3 PREREQUISITE NOT MET; last 10 derived gate families and the dogfood battery NOT MEASURED locally" — answered: the head's check-runs are the gate verdicts; none that completed failed, and the remaining families are the 12 runs still in progress. No local re-run (read-only).
- "`check:engine-double-contract` exit 1 then 0 after `--write`" — answered: the ledger is committed in the head, gate green locally per the record and in CI's lint set.
- `sys_audit_log` in plugin-security's shipped `organization_admin` sets is not registered when plugin-audit is absent — answered by the held-grant exemption (0 shipped sets refused on re-save, measured over three boots per ruling 2). A NEW set granting on it in such a boot is refused: that is the ruling's "known is the runtime's view" and the grant would apply to nothing there.
- No `open_questions` entry on the card or the PR. The seat's wrap-up stopped the os-dev-report; the PR body carries the readings.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing makes the spec's own refusal real at the consumer: `collectPermissionGrantObjectErrors` (#18202) refuses the same grant at `defineStack` with the sentence this door now opens with; the runtime save was the one path that stored it. No declared capability is taken away: `PermissionSetSchema.objects` declares a map keyed by object name, and a key naming no object grants nothing (the evaluator indexes by name), so nothing a consumer could rely on is lost. The one divergence from the build rule is deliberate and sound: the build passes any `sys_`/`cloud_`/`ai_` prefix because the build cannot see the registry; at runtime the registry is authoritative, so platform objects pass by registration (pinned on `sys_user_position`) and a prefixed name nothing registers is refused as the typo it is.

Tried to break it:
- Draft granting on an object draft from another package, then the per-item publish or this package's batch → refused (object not in the batch, not stored); the object's own publish first unblocks it. Correct, same as #26724.
- Re-save of a set holding a stale grant plus a new typo → the stale key passes, the typo is refused (pinned). The exemption cannot be used to sneak a new unknown key in.
- Legacy FQN `crm__lead` as a grant key → `getObject` answers the object named `lead`/`crm_lead`, `.name !== key` → refused; the evaluator would never match it. Correct.
- Restore door receives no `pending`/`writeFace` → judged against the active set only, as the datasource refusal is. Correct.
- Order at the save door: after the schema gate and the datasource refusal, before the credentialsRef refusal, the authoring gate and every write; at the promotion before `repo.promoteDraft`, so a batch publish aborts. Correct.

Should-fix (not blocking): the finding's second clause ("none is saved here") is literally true on the save path but, on the publish path, the object may well be stored as a draft outside this batch; "and no published object or object draft of this batch" would name the publish case exactly. Wording only; the first sentence (the build rule's) and the path are what the tests and Studio key on.

No must-fix.
